THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
 -5-  NC: 2024:KHC:45854  WP No. 21970 of 2024 CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE B M SHYAM PRASAD  ORAL ORDER
The petitioners are the owners of certain immovable properties in Kothanuru village, Uttarahalli Hobli, J.P.Nagar, 8th Phase, Bengaluru.

They are aggrieved by the Notification dated 15.03.2024 [Annexure-A] issued by the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike [BBMP] proposing to acquire their properties and other properties for developing a 24 meter-Wide Road.
Sri R.S. Prasanna Kumar, the learned counsel for the petitioners, proposes to canvass multiple grounds to assert why the BBMP could not have issued the Notification.

Sri Pawan Kumar, the learned standing counsel for the third and sixth respondents, submits that:
[i] the impugned Notification is not for acquisition of the property as is contemplated under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land NC:
2024:KHC:45854 Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, but it is only to invite consent from those who are willing to agree to give portions of their lands for road widening in consideration for Development Right, [ii] if the petitioners do not wish to consent, the authorities depending on the exigencies that could be and Sri Gireesh Kamath H vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69635696/
4 in the public interest will decide to acquire lands.

Therefore, the petition stands disposed of without prejudice to the State to issue Notification for acquisition of lands for road widening leaving open all questions to be considered if there is occasion for the same.
